match.reason: None of the bank points teaches that Australian English has borrowed words from many languages, including Aboriginal languages; the closest, on spelling patterns from French and Greek, is narrower and about spelling rather than borrowing.

draft.title: Words Australian English has borrowed
card: Languages borrow words from each other, and English has done this for centuries. Australian English has borrowed words from many languages.
Aboriginal languages
Many Australian place names and animal names come from Aboriginal languages. Kangaroo comes from Guugu Yimithirr, a language of far north Queensland. Other examples are koala and wombat.
French
English took many words from French, such as menu, ballet and restaurant. Many of these came into English long before English reached Australia.
Greek and Latin
Many English words are built from Greek and Latin parts. Telephone has Greek parts that mean far and sound. Library comes from the Latin word liber, which means book.
draft.remember: Australian English is a mix of borrowed words, from Aboriginal languages, French, Greek, Latin and more.

a.q: The word kangaroo came into English from which source?
opts: The Guugu Yimithirr language of far north Queensland
The French language
The Greek language
The Latin language
a.why: Kangaroo was borrowed from Guugu Yimithirr, an Aboriginal language of far north Queensland. French, Greek and Latin gave English many other words, but not this one.
a.clue: Think of an Australian animal and an Aboriginal language.

b.q: Ravi notices that the word telephone is built from Greek parts meaning far and sound. What does this show about English?
opts: It has borrowed and built words from Greek
It borrowed telephone from an Aboriginal language
It borrowed telephone directly from French
It has never borrowed words from other languages
b.why: Telephone is made from Greek parts, so it shows English borrowing from Greek. The other options name the wrong source or deny that English borrows at all.
b.clue: Look at where the parts of the word come from.

a.best: The Guugu Yimithirr language of far north Queensland

b.best: It has borrowed and built words from Greek

problems.detail: 'Many of these came into English long before English reached Australia' sits under the examples menu, ballet and restaurant, but restaurant (about the 1820s) and menu (about the 1830s) entered English after English reached Australia in 1788. Only ballet fits. Use examples that do fit, such as beef, castle or justice, or drop the claim.

'Australian English is a mix of borrowed words' suggests the whole language is borrowed. The card says only that it 'has borrowed words from many languages', and English has a large native core. Reword to something like 'Australian English includes words borrowed from...'.

The right option is clearly the longest and the only one with precise detail ('of far north Queensland'). The clue's 'Aboriginal language' also points straight to it, since it is the only non-European option. A student could pick it without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: Words Australian English has borrowed
card: Languages borrow words from each other, and English has done this for centuries. Australian English has borrowed words from many languages.
Aboriginal languages
Many Australian place names and animal names come from Aboriginal languages. Kangaroo comes from Guugu Yimithirr, a language of far north Queensland. Other examples are koala and wombat.
French
English took many words from French, such as beef, pork and justice. These came in after French-speaking Normans conquered England in 1066, long before English reached Australia.
Greek and Latin
Many English words are built from Greek and Latin parts. Telephone has Greek parts that mean far and sound. Library goes back to the Latin word liber, which means book.
proposal.remember: Australian English includes words borrowed from Aboriginal languages, French, Greek, Latin and more.
